comparator.sourceNotes: The programme is taught in English at VU Amsterdam's School of Business and Economics and carries 180 EC over three years. The complete 180-EC pathway is taken from the formally adopted 2026-2027 SBE bachelor Teaching and Examination Regulations and their annual programme schedule for International Business Administration, cross-checked against the current official programme and curriculum pages. Year 1 consists of ten compulsory 6-EC courses; year 2 of eight compulsory 6-EC courses plus one 6-EC restricted-choice elective in period 4 and one in period 5; year 3 of a mandatory 30-EC international exchange semester, compulsory Ethics (6 EC), two 6-EC courses of one chosen specialization and a 12-EC bachelor's thesis written within that specialization. The compulsory zero-credit components (Mentoring Programme (SAM), the English language test and Research Participation I and II) carry no EC and are therefore outside the 180-EC component list. The eleven year-3 specializations are equally general deepening options rather than formal programme routes that define the target's academic identity, and the normalized target is the generic bachelor, so no route is named and the specialization and elective spaces are preserved as restricted choice instead of being instantiated. One discrepancy was found and resolved in favour of the formally adopted source: the interest evidence recorded for this target lists international business law as curriculum content, but in the 2026-2027 schedule International Business Law is one of the six period-4 electives, not a compulsory course, so it is represented inside the restricted-choice elective space rather than as a compulsory component.

components.note: Restricted choice: one of the six period-4 options listed in the formally adopted 2026-2027 SBE programme schedule (Global Marketing Innovation, International Business Law, Digital Innovation and Virtual Organizing in a Global Setting, Managing People: A Global Perspective, Sustainable Management of Global Supply Chains, IBA Lab I). The space is preserved as restricted choice rather than instantiated with one option.

components.name: Elective, period 5
components.note: Restricted choice: one of the four period-5 options listed in the formally adopted 2026-2027 SBE programme schedule (IBA Lab II, Inclusive Growth and Sustainability, Corporate Finance: A Sustainability Perspective, Accounting, Business and Society). IBA Lab II additionally requires enrolment in IBA Lab I in period 4.

components.name: International exchange semester
components.note: Mandatory international exchange semester at one of more than 150 partner universities on six continents; the credits are earned abroad and the specific course content is not fixed by the VU curriculum.

components.name: Specialization course, period 4
components.note: Restricted choice: one 6-EC course of the chosen year-3 specialization, on which the thesis is also written. The 2026-2027 programme schedule offers eleven equally general specializations (Accounting, Digital Business Innovation, Economics, Entrepreneurship, Finance, Financial Management, Management Consulting, Marketing, Strategic Human Resource Management / Leadership and Change Management, Strategy and Organization, Transport and Supply Chain Management); none is more representative of the programme's broad academic identity, so the space is preserved as restricted choice and no specialization is instantiated.

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to the VU International Business Administration target: the business-administration core of the external programme rebuilt from UCR's Business & Entrepreneurship cluster, combining business and entrepreneurship foundations, micro- and macroeconomics, accounting and finance, marketing and consumer engagement, strategy and digital transformation, the international business environment and its legal frameworks, organisational behaviour and diversity management, and a quantitative and qualitative research-methods sequence. UCR offers no supply-chain management and no business mathematics course, so those parts of the VU core are not reproduced.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum contains eight economics, accounting and finance courses, four marketing, strategy and international-business courses, four leadership and organisational-behaviour courses, four methods and data courses and two law courses, so the label names that combination rather than presenting the programme as a management degree or as an economics degree. It deliberately does not claim supply-chain management, which the programme does not contain.

alternatives.concept: A related direction built on the target's own explicit commitment to sustainability, responsible decision-making and corporate responsibility across cultures: it keeps the business, economics, accounting and finance foundations and the international operating environment, and then organises the upper years around what responsible conduct actually requires — sustainability science and circular production, the governance of sustainability, public and behavioural economics, transnational business law, ethics and the civil-society claims firms answer to. Its organising logic is the firm's responsibility for its impact rather than the general administration of the firm.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Alternative 1 reproduces the administration of an international firm: it spends its upper years on marketing, market research, econometrics, strategy and digital transformation. Alternative 2 starts from the target's own question about how cultures view corporate social responsibility and responsible finance and answers it with the material that makes responsibility assessable: sustainability science and the evidential discipline of Sustainability Essentials II, lifecycle and circular-production analysis, recycling and remediation, climate change, the governance of sustainability, public economics and social-movement and environmental-justice sociology. The consequence is curricular, not cosmetic: eight of twenty-four courses differ, the entire marketing, market-research and econometrics block of Alternative 1 is absent, and Alternative 1's single sustainability course is replaced by a six-course sustainability and governance sequence.

alternatives.concept: A question-led programme built on the target's own example of how a product can be introduced to consumers in an unfamiliar cultural market: it keeps the business, economics and research-methods foundations and the international operating environment, and then organises the programme around consumer behaviour and consumer psychology, marketing and market research, product development, the sociology of the societies in which markets are embedded, and the rhetoric and stylistics of persuasive communication. Its organising method is empirical and interpretive analysis of consumers and cultures rather than the administration of the firm.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Alternative 1 administers the firm and Alternative 2 asks what the firm is responsible for; Alternative 3 asks how a product and a brand actually travel into a market whose culture the firm does not share. That question changes the curriculum rather than its label: nine of twenty-four courses differ from Alternative 1 and fourteen from Alternative 2. Accounting, finance, econometrics, sustainability and the whole leadership sequence give way to consumer product design, social psychology, behavioural economics, four sociology courses on how societies and modern market cultures are constituted, and three courses on rhetoric, stylistics and the ethics of persuasion, with market research and qualitative methodology retained as the empirical means of studying consumers.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Economics and Law, Society & Justice open semester one and Research Methods & Statistics follows in semester two, so both gateway courses precede every course that formally requires them and the legal foundation precedes Transnational Business Law in semester four. Accounting & Corporate Finance precedes Money, Banking & Finance; Introduction to Economics precedes International Macroeconomics, Microeconomics & Behavior and Econometrics; Personal Leadership precedes Psychology of Organizations & Leadership; and Research Methods & Statistics and Statistics & Experimental Methods both precede Econometrics and Market Research. Every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester and every course is offered in the term it is assigned to.

basisLabels: International business administration: how firms are organised, managed and operated across borders
courseTraceability.rationale: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations builds a new venture from ideation through to a final pitch and teaches design thinking, market validation and business planning, which is the practical business-foundations work the VU programme places in its first-year core. It implements the explicit academic basis “International business administration: how firms are organised, managed and operated across borders”.

basisLabels: Global economics: micro- and macroeconomic principles applied to an integrated world economy
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Economics teaches the micro- and macroeconomic principles the programme's global-economics strand depends on, from consumer and firm theory and market structure to aggregate output, unemployment, inflation and the short-run behaviour of goods and financial markets. It implements the explicit academic basis “Global economics: micro- and macroeconomic principles applied to an integrated world economy”.

basisLabels: Legal frameworks governing cross-border business
courseTraceability.rationale: Law, Society & Justice sets out the legal systems, constitutional, administrative, criminal, international, property, contract and tort law that a cross-border business curriculum presupposes, and practises them through case law and trial simulations. It implements the explicit academic basis “Legal frameworks governing cross-border business”.

basisLabels: Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project
courseTraceability.rationale: Research Methods & Statistics delivers the research-design and statistics training the programme requires, covering operationalization, sampling, experimental design, survey and laboratory research and descriptive and inferential statistics up to analysis of variance. It implements the explicit academic basis “Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project”.

basisLabels: International strategy, digital technologies and the responsible use of AI in business
courseTraceability.rationale: Strategy & Digital Transformation develops a strategic plan from vision to execution and analyses how digital technology change reshapes strategy, business models and corporate social responsibility. It implements the explicit academic basis “International strategy, digital technologies and the responsible use of AI in business”.

basisLabels: Ethics, corporate social responsibility and sustainability in global business
courseTraceability.rationale: Ethics works through virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism and applies them to practical questions of equality, poverty and wealth, future generations and climate change, which is the moral-reasoning training behind the programme's compulsory ethics course. It implements the explicit academic basis “Ethics, corporate social responsibility and sustainability in global business”.

basisLabels: Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project
courseTraceability.rationale: Qualitative Research Methodology teaches the full qualitative research cycle of design, data collection and management, interpretation and dissemination, which is the qualitative business-research method the programme requires. It implements the explicit academic basis “Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project”.

basisLabels: Accounting, corporate finance and financial decision-making
courseTraceability.rationale: Accounting & Corporate Finance teaches students to comprehend a corporate annual report, to analyse financial statements and to use accounting to trace how economic events affect a business. It implements the explicit academic basis “Accounting, corporate finance and financial decision-making”.

basisLabels: Global economics: micro- and macroeconomic principles applied to an integrated world economy
courseTraceability.rationale: International Macroeconomics analyses national income, growth, inflation and unemployment, the effect of fiscal and monetary policy, business cycles, economic crises and international trade, the macroeconomic material behind the programme's economics in a global era. It implements the explicit academic basis “Global economics: micro- and macroeconomic principles applied to an integrated world economy”.

basisLabels: People in business and society: organisational behaviour, leadership and the management of diverse teams
courseTraceability.rationale: Personal Leadership introduces leadership theory with an emphasis on self-awareness, goal-setting and emotional intelligence, the personal-leadership foundation on which the programme's people-in-business strand builds. It implements the explicit academic basis “People in business and society: organisational behaviour, leadership and the management of diverse teams”.

basisLabels: Ethics, corporate social responsibility and sustainability in global business

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three UCR alternatives are defensible and the maximum was reached. Alternative 1 is the closest feasible response to the VU target: it rebuilds the business-administration core from UCR's Business & Entrepreneurship cluster but cannot reproduce the programme's supply-chain management, business mathematics or information-systems courses, its exchange semester or its thesis. Alternative 2 follows the target's own explicit commitment to sustainability, responsible decision-making and corporate social responsibility across cultures and turns it into a programme about what responsible conduct requires, differing from Alternative 1 in eight of twenty-four courses. Alternative 3 follows the target's own example of introducing a product to consumers in an unfamiliar cultural market and answers it with consumer behaviour, sociology of markets and persuasive communication, differing from Alternative 1 in nine courses and from Alternative 2 in fourteen. A fourth direction, leading and building trust in diverse and virtual international teams, was assessed: its evidence is already substantively carried by the closest-match core, which schedules Personal Leadership, Leadership & Diversity Management and Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, and no genuinely different 24-course curriculum follows from it, so it was not advanced as a fourth candidate. No alternative was manufactured to reach three.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both teach the core academic skills of selecting and critically analysing sources, articulating research questions and arguments and writing and presenting academically. The UCR course adds personal and civic development and community engagement, which the VU course does not.

Both teach the statistics a business student needs, from descriptive measures to inferential testing, together with the research design in which they are used. The UCR course combines methodology and statistics in one course rather than separating them.

Both teach the quantitative analysis used in empirical research on people, including regression, analysis of variance and further multivariate models. The UCR course is set in the health and behavioural sciences rather than in business.

Both teach qualitative research: design, data collection and management, interpretation of meaning and dissemination. The VU course applies this to business questions; the UCR course applies it to social processes.

Both require students to integrate evidence in a complete empirical research project: designing it, collecting and analysing data and reporting the result. The VU project is discipline-general, while the UCR course carries out that project as market research.

UCR offers no business mathematics course. Mathematical Methods exists in the Data Science & Intelligent Systems cluster but is not part of any of these three programmes, and no scheduled course teaches calculus, algebra or mathematical modelling for business, so the row stays blank rather than being filled with a statistics course.

The 12-EC bachelor's thesis, written inside the chosen specialization, has no counterpart among the 24 scheduled UCR courses: none of these programmes contains a thesis. Independent research appears instead as the standardized optional 15-EC comparison element shown alongside this component.

Both concern managing people, and both treat cultural and individual difference as the central practical problem of doing so. The VU course builds that on psychological foundations, while the UCR course works from leadership theory and diversity management.

Both examine how organisations work: structure, culture, motivation, group dynamics, power and decision-making. The VU course approaches this as organisation theory, while the UCR course works from organisational psychology and behaviour, so it covers the behavioural half of the subject at 300 level rather than the theory of organisational design as such.

Both study how people think, feel and behave in the presence of others as the basis for understanding behaviour in organisations and markets. The VU course frames that material as people in business and society; the UCR course teaches it as social psychology and does not take the firm as its setting.

No scheduled UCR course teaches the design, management and improvement of business processes. Consumer Product Design covers one product-development process and Strategy & Digital Transformation covers business-model change, but neither addresses business-process management as a subject, so the row stays blank.

Both teach economic principles as the foundation of the programme, covering consumer and firm behaviour, market structure and the main macroeconomic aggregates. The VU course frames those principles for a global era, a framing the UCR programmes carry in International Macroeconomics.

Both teach accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on reading and analysing financial statements and annual reports. The UCR course additionally covers corporate finance, which the VU programme places in a separate second-year Finance course.

Both teach financial decision-making: analysing financial data, assessing risk and making investment, budgeting and funding decisions. The UCR course is a 300-level case-based course that also covers money and banking.

Both teach strategy formation, from analysis and vision through to execution, and both examine how business models change. The VU course frames strategy internationally, while the UCR course frames it around digital transformation; the international dimension is carried separately by International Business & Governance.

Both study marketing strategy and what drives consumer behaviour and engagement with brands. The VU course foregrounds cultural difference across markets, while the UCR course foregrounds consumer psychology, brand strategy and digital and AI-driven marketing.

UCR teaches no supply-chain management. Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy and R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation examine material flows for their environmental impact, not the planning, sourcing and logistics of a global supply chain, so no scheduled UCR course is a sufficiently direct counterpart and the row stays blank.

Both establish what sustainability means and which planetary limits economic activity operates within, as a first-year foundation for later sustainability work. The VU course does so from a business perspective; the UCR gateway course does so from sustainability science.

Both are dedicated ethics courses that teach the main normative theories and then apply them to contested practical questions. The VU course applies them to business, while the UCR course applies them to equality, poverty, future generations and climate change.

Both concern turning organisational data into usable information, and both require students to work hands-on with data and report a result. The VU course studies information systems as business infrastructure, while the UCR course teaches data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation; UCR does not teach enterprise information systems.

notes.text: Both the VU programme and the UCR programmes include substantial study of international business, economics, finance, marketing and research methods. The International Business Administration programme additionally includes specialist work in global supply chain management, business mathematics, business information systems and a mandatory 30-EC exchange semester, and it ends with a specialization and a bachelor's thesis in one business discipline. UCR students can instead combine the international business and governance, economics, marketing, data science, sustainability and law courses shown here, but those specialist components are not offered at UCR and independent research appears only as an optional element.

The VU programme organises study around a fixed sequence of compulsory 6-EC business courses, two restricted-choice electives, a mandatory semester abroad and a chosen year-3 specialization with a thesis. At UCR, comparable subjects are distributed across individually chosen 7.5-EC courses in business and entrepreneurship, government and society, media, culture and communication, environment and sustainability, and data science, with four courses in each of six semesters. The UCR programmes therefore cover related territory through a different curricular structure rather than reproducing the external programme course by course.
